name: Weighted spider fusion
summary: Two connected white (Z) spiders with labels r and s fuse into one with label rs.
description:
In the $R$-labelled ZW-calculus the white spider with label $r$ is $|0\cdots0\rangle + r|1\cdots1\rangle$, which in PyZX is a Z-box with label $r$. Two connected white spiders fuse, and their labels multiply. For two-legged spiders this is the axiom $rng_\times^{r,s}$: composing $\mathrm{diag}(1, r)$ and $\mathrm{diag}(1, s)$ gives $\mathrm{diag}(1, rs)$; the [sum rule](../w-sum/) provides addition.

With $r = e^{i\alpha}$ and $s = e^{i\beta}$ this is ordinary spider fusion of the ZX-calculus.
parameter_notes: Shown for two spiders with two outer legs each; holds for any number of legs.

source.location: Chapter 5, Section 5.2 (list of rules of the ZW calculus), rule $cut_z$
